title: Abysmal performance from SVG Thumbnail Provider
author: callmeTayyy
summary: SVG thumbnail generation takes about two seconds per file because each request creates and tears down a WebView2 rendering environment and process.

status.label: Actionable SVG thumbnail design
status.detail: The report, videos, and code-path analysis identify per-thumbnail browser startup as the dominant cost.

next_action.label: Approve SVG renderer design investigation
next_action.reason: Choose and validate a renderer/lifetime strategy that preserves SVG fidelity without a browser startup per file.

judgment.rationale: The failure is reproducible with a large SVG folder, and the latest investigation identifies the expensive lifecycle boundary. A bounded design can compare renderer reuse or replacement without requesting more generic logs.
evidence: The reporter measured roughly two seconds per thumbnail and observed a WebView2 process for each SVG.
The latest contributor traced each request through WebView2 creation, render, image capture, and disposal.
The discussion identifies fidelity limits of Direct2D and packaging/toolchain costs of alternative renderers.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused design and benchmark the current lifecycle against a reusable or non-WebView2 renderer.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix attempt exists; the public analysis supports a repository change at the SVG thumbnail renderer lifecycle.

proposed_fixes.title: Avoid per-thumbnail WebView2 startup for SVG thumbnails
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The SVG thumbnail provider pays WebView2 environment, process, user-data, rendering, capture, and cleanup costs for each individual thumbnail request.
plan: Instrument the SVG thumbnail provider to separate WebView2 startup, navigation/render, capture, resize, and cleanup time.
Prototype the lowest-risk lifecycle reuse boundary allowed by the out-of-process thumbnail host and compare it with a native renderer option on representative SVG features.
Preserve a fidelity fallback for text, CSS, filters, foreignObject, and embedded-font cases that a faster renderer cannot handle.
Add performance coverage for a cold cache folder with at least 100 SVGs and correctness fixtures for complex SVG features.
verification: Clear the thumbnail cache and measure time/process creation for 100 representative SVG files.
Confirm complex text, CSS, filter, and foreignObject samples remain visually correct.
Verify Explorer host isolation and cleanup after cancellation or process termination.

confidence.rationale: The expensive lifecycle is directly identified, but the safe reuse boundary and fidelity-compatible renderer choice require maintainer benchmarking.

issue_context.summary: Large SVG folders generate thumbnails slowly and spawn many WebView2/provider processes.
known_information: The report includes comparative videos, hardware details, and a diagnostic archive.
Each SVG request currently creates and discards a WebView2 renderer.
Native renderer alternatives differ materially in SVG feature support and packaging cost.
inferences: Removing repeated browser startup should improve throughput substantially, but replacing WebView2 outright could regress complex SVG fidelity.
issue_context.analysis: The remaining uncertainty is an engineering tradeoff best reduced by local profiling and fidelity fixtures, not additional reporter diagnostics.
initial_investigation: Read all issue comments and linked similar-issue references.
Used the latest contributor's code-path analysis to identify the per-request lifecycle cost.
Compared the stated renderer alternatives and their known fidelity/toolchain constraints.

actions.label: Benchmark SVG thumbnail generation

prerequisites: Use the latest stable or Preview PowerToys build in a disposable test environment.
steps: Open a folder containing at least 100 representative SVG files.
Record thumbnail completion time and count new PowerToys.SvgThumbnailProvider.exe and msedgewebview2.exe processes.
Profile startup, render, capture, and cleanup phases in a local instrumented build.
reproduce.expected: A candidate design materially reduces process creation and total rendering time while preserving output for complex SVG fixtures.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Create a non-sensitive corpus of at least 100 SVGs including paths, gradients, live text, CSS, filters, foreignObject, and embedded fonts; record per-feature expected thumbnails.

actions.note: Local maintainer investigation only; this action performs no upstream write.
